main_topics.reason: The user described frequent bowel movements, occasional blood, and urgency with almost no warning as the main problem affecting daily life.
The user asked what to discuss after learning their symptoms may not be controlled on mesalamine and asked specifically whether rectal treatment could help.
The user said specialist appointments were hard to get and asked how to get one faster; arranging a referral became part of the plan.
The user said urgency affected their job and asked for ways to cope with fear of needing the bathroom during meetings.
The user began ashamed to discuss the symptoms and later expressed anger about having believed they were normal.
The user asked whether the stool test could show inflammation without a colonoscopy and received an explanation of its use.
The user felt they might be complaining too much and worried about sounding stupid, then asked what to ask the doctor.
The user said they had loperamide at home and were considering taking it, then agreed to ask their doctor first.

output.summary: The user described ulcerative colitis symptoms, including frequent urgent bowel movements and occasional blood, that were affecting work and family life, and said they had assumed this was simply normal. The assistant discussed specialist review, possible treatment options, calprotectin testing, and practical coping measures, while advising the user to check with a doctor before taking loperamide. The user said they felt less ashamed and had a plan for what to ask and do next.
